requirements.text:
clamp(x, lo, hi) reads its arguments as signed integers. It returns lo when x < lo, else hi
when x > hi, else x.
requirements.reason: It covers all 32-bit inputs, compares them as signed values, and returns lo, hi, or x according to the required conditions. The examples confirm signed interpretation, including 4294967295 as −1.

requirements.text:
gcd(a, b) reads its arguments as unsigned integers and returns their greatest common divisor,
with gcd(a, 0) = a.
requirements.reason: It computes the greatest common divisor over the unsigned values of both inputs for every pair, including gcd(a, 0) = a. The examples include gcd(0, 6) → 6.

requirements.text: sum_to(n) reads n as an unsigned integer and returns 0 + 1 + ... + (n - 1), wrapped to 32 bits.
requirements.reason: It covers every 32-bit input as an unsigned natural and returns the sum from 0 through n−1 modulo 2³². The examples confirm the empty sum at n=0 and the sequence for small inputs.

claims.summary: The sum_to export returns the sum of the integers below its 32-bit input, modulo 2³².
claims.name: Examples.Toy.sumTo
claims.intent: `sum_to(n)` on unsigned 32-bit ints: `0 + 1 + … + (n − 1)`, wrapped to 32 bits.
details: Covers every 32-bit input; the input is interpreted as an unsigned natural number for the range and sum.
The expected result is the sum of all integers from zero up to, but not including, that unsigned input, reduced modulo 2³².
Returns additionally guarantees the module can be instantiated and that every call under every host behavior terminates without a trap and returns exactly the stated value.

claims.summary: The clamp export returns the lower bound if the value is signed-smaller, otherwise the upper bound if it is signed-smaller than the value, and otherwise the value.
claims.statement:
∀ (x lo hi : BitVec 32),
  FVA.Wasm.Exec.Returns Examples.Toy.Lifted.module "clamp"
    [FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 x, FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 lo, FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 hi]
    [FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 (if x.slt lo = true then lo else if hi.slt x = true then hi else x)]
claims.name: Examples.Toy.clamp
claims.intent:
`clamp(x, lo, hi)` on signed 32-bit ints: `lo` if `x < lo`, else `hi` if `x > hi`, else `x`
(tested in this order, so with `lo > hi` the result is `lo` for `x < lo` and `hi` otherwise).
details: Covers every combination of three 32-bit inputs: the value, lower bound, and upper bound.
Comparisons interpret each input as a signed 32-bit integer; the returned value is one of the original inputs, so no arithmetic wraparound occurs.
Returns additionally guarantees the module can be instantiated and that every call under every host behavior terminates without a trap and returns exactly the stated value.
caveats: This does not require the lower bound to be less than or equal to the upper bound; when the bounds are reversed, the stated comparison order still determines the result.
The comparisons are signed, even though the inputs are 32-bit bit patterns.

claims.summary: The gcd export returns the greatest common divisor of its two inputs interpreted as unsigned 32-bit integers.
claims.statement:
∀ (a b : BitVec 32),
  FVA.Wasm.Exec.Returns Examples.Toy.Lifted.module "gcd" [FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 a, FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 b]
    [FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 (BitVec.ofNat 32 (a.toNat.gcd b.toNat))]
claims.name: Examples.Toy.gcd
claims.intent: `gcd(a, b)` on unsigned 32-bit ints: their greatest common divisor (`gcd(a, 0) = a`).
details: Covers every pair of 32-bit inputs, each converted to an unsigned natural number before computing the greatest common divisor.
The result is encoded as a 32-bit value; there is no intermediate 32-bit arithmetic wraparound in the natural-number greatest-common-divisor calculation.
Returns additionally guarantees the module can be instantiated and that every call under every host behavior terminates without a trap and returns exactly the stated value.
caveats: The inputs are treated as unsigned magnitudes, not signed integers; negative example values denote their 32-bit bit patterns.
The result is reduced modulo 2³², though the greatest common divisor of these unsigned inputs already fits in 32 bits.
